reference_use.conclusion: The pinned SimonGMT has covectors, forms, test forms, currents and covectorEuclideanNorm. It has no continuity lemma for pulled-back forms and no mollification of covector-valued fields. Its convolution code (Chapter02/BV, WhitneyPartition, Chapter08) is scalar and not imported by the contract. No DAG declaration has the three child types. The nearest accepted ones work in covectorEuclideanNorm: dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field (needs |g| ≤ 1, fixed ε) and part (d) of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (bound on |ξ(α)|). So all three children are new, and the names dtc_bc_lc_pf_ext_* are unused in dag.json and git history. The frozen imports exclude ContDiffBump.normed, so the mollification normalizes the bump by hand and uses dist_convolution_le, as the accepted candidate 8abce32 does. Measurability of ξ(G) needs Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply. All three types elaborate in the comparator scope, and complete Lean proofs of all three use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The exact frozen parent type is proved in Lean from them plus the carrier_facts dependency; the only sorry is the placeholder for that queued dependency.

rationale:
Split into three new, independent lemmas with no sibling dependencies. The selected node is at depth 5 (limit 6), so the children are leaves; each one was checked to be provable as stated. Each child is one obligation of the supplied proof and is reusable on its own:
1. pullback_cutoff, dtc_bc_lc_pf_ext_pullback_cutoff (supplied steps 1–2). Let f be C¹ on an open O ⊇ K, K compact, and ω a continuous form on ℝ^Q. Then there is a continuous, compactly supported covector field h on ℝ^P with h = ω(f)∘Df on K. The lemma is stated for maps ℝ^P → ℝ^Q and any continuous ω; the parent uses Q = P and its test form.
2. mollify, dtc_bc_lc_pf_ext_mollify_tendstoUniformly (step 3). A continuous, compactly supported covector field is the uniform limit of test forms in TestFormOn univ n.
3. integral_limit, dtc_bc_lc_pf_ext_imrep_integral_tendsto (steps 4(b)–(c), the integrability part of 5, and 6). Let R : IMRep U n and let K ⊆ U be compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. If continuous g_j → g uniformly on K, then ∫_M θξ(g_j) dHⁿ → ∫_M θξ(g) dHⁿ.

How the children give the selected statement by the supplied proof (also checked in Lean):
- Fix P, n, O, K, f, ω. Apply pullback_cutoff with Q := P and the form ω, which is continuous because IsTestForm gives ContDiff ℝ ∞. This gives h. Apply mollify to h; this gives ωs.
- The sequence ωs depends only on f, ω, O and K, not on Y or R (step 3(c)).
- Let Y, R satisfy R.Represents Y and Y.support ⊆ K. The node's existing dependency carrier_facts, part (1), gives Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0, hence Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (step 4(a)).
- Apply integral_limit with U = univ, gs j = ωs j, g = h, and TendstoUniformly.tendstoUniformlyOn. This gives ∫θξ(ωs j) → ∫θξ(h).
- Y(ωs j) = R.action(ωs j), which is that integral, by R.Represents and the definition of IMRep.action (step 5).
- ∫θξ(h) = ∫θξ(ω(f)∘Df) by integral_congr_ae, because h = ω(f)∘Df on K and Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in K (step 5).
The parent assembly is about 25 Lean lines.

Why split rather than prove the theorem in one piece:
- The three parts are mathematically independent: calculus and topology, convolution, and measure theory.
- Each part has its own Lean pitfall. The frozen imports exclude ContDiffBump.normed and dist_normed_convolution_le, so the bump must be normalized by hand and dist_convolution_le used instead. Measurability of x ↦ ξ(x)(G(x)) needs Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply, because of the topology instance on MultiVector.
- The lemmas are reusable, for example by the twin node dimred_mbl_pf_pullback_integral_extension, which has a byte-identical frozen type.

No accepted declaration has these exact types. The nearest are dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field (an ε-approximation in covectorEuclideanNorm, requiring |g| ≤ 1) and part (d) of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (a bound on |ξ(α)| in covectorEuclideanNorm). Adapting them would need extra scaling and norm-comparison lemmas, while the operator-norm argument of the supplied proof is short. So all three children are new and nothing is reused. The bound tsupport ω_j ⊆ tsupport h + B̄(0, 1) in step 3(a) is not used by steps 4–6, so it is omitted.

Checks:
- All three types elaborate in the comparator scope (namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens).
- validate_lean_statement accepts all three strings.
- Complete Lean proofs of all three children compile at the pinned toolchain using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
- A Lean proof of the exact frozen parent type compiles from these children plus the carrier_facts type. The only sorryAx comes from the placeholder for that queued dependency.
- The new names are unused in dag.json and in the git history.

subproblems.title: Cut-off of the pulled-back form: a continuous compactly supported covector field equal to ω(f(x))∘Df(x) on K
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O), and ω : ℝ^Q → Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) a continuous n-form (DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n). Then there is a continuous, compactly supported covector field h : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) n) with h(x) = ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) for every x ∈ K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid Q) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) n), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → Continuous ω → ∃ h : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous h ∧ HasCompactSupport h ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, h x = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof. This is the cut-off ζ of Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (chapter-06.txt lines 408–412: ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) identically one in a neighbourhood of the compact set spt T ∩ spt f^#ω), applied to the pulled-back form x ↦ ω(f(x))∘Df(x) of 2.24(2) (lines 415–424), which makes sense for f merely C¹. Two harmless generalizations of the parent's setting: the target space is ℝ^Q (the parent uses Q = P), and ω is any continuous n-form on ℝ^Q (the parent's test form is C^∞, hence continuous). Only continuity of the cut-off is used.
Notation: Λⁿ(V) := Covector V n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps Vⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm. Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q). γ(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P), so γ(x)(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ). thickening(r, K) := {x : infEdist(x, K) < r} is open; cthickening(r, K) := {x : infEdist(x, K) ≤ r} is closed.
1. f and Df are continuous on O. Since f is C¹ on O, f is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Since O is open and 1 ≤ 1, Df = fderiv ℝ f is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen hf hO le_rfl).
2. The pull-back map is continuous. Let Φ : Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) × L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) → Λⁿ(ℝ^P), Φ(β, A) := β.compContinuousLinearMap A. Mathlib shows Φ has a strict Fréchet derivative at every point (ContinuousAlternatingMap.hasStrictFDerivAt_compContinuousLinearMap), and such a map is continuous at that point (HasStrictFDerivAt.continuousAt). So Φ is continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt). Equivalently, Φ(β, A) = compContinuousLinearMapCLM A β, where A ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM A is continuous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM) and evaluation is jointly continuous; in coordinates Φ is a polynomial in the entries of β and A.
3. γ is continuous on O. x ↦ ω(f(x)) is continuous on O, since ω is continuous and f is continuous on O (Continuous.comp_continuousOn). With step 1, x ↦ (ω(f(x)), Df(x)) is continuous on O (ContinuousOn.prodMk). So γ = Φ ∘ (x ↦ (ω(f(x)), Df(x))) is continuous on O by step 2.
4. Margin. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is ρ > 0 with cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); write ρ = 2δ. The set cthickening(ρ, K) is compact, because K is compact and ℝ^P is proper (IsCompact.cthickening).
5. Cut-off. Let s := thickening(ρ, K), which is open, and t := cthickening(ρ/2, K), which is closed. Since 0 < ρ/2 < ρ, t ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening'). Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma in the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff) to the open s and the closed t ⊆ s, with any smoothness order, e.g. 0. This gives χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with values in [0, 1], continuous (ContDiff.continuous), support χ = s, and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ t. A continuous Urysohn function, e.g. from exists_tsupport_one_of_isOpen_isClosed, would serve equally well. Then:
 (a) χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K, because K ⊆ t (self_subset_cthickening);
 (b) tsupport χ = closure(s) ⊆ cthickening(ρ, K) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening). Hence tsupport χ ⊆ O by step 4, and tsupport χ lies in the compact set cthickening(ρ, K).
6. Definition. For every x ∈ ℝ^P put h(x) := χ(x)·γ(x) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P), using scalar multiplication in Λⁿ(ℝ^P). γ(x) is defined for every x through fderiv, but is controlled only on O.
7. h has compact support. If χ(x) = 0 then h(x) = 0, so tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ (tsupport_smul_subset_left). tsupport h is closed and contained in the compact set cthickening(ρ, K) (step 5(b)), so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). That is, HasCompactSupport h.
8. h is continuous. On O, h is the product of the continuous real function χ and the function γ, which is continuous on O by step 3; so h is continuous on O (ContinuousOn.smul). Also tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O by steps 5(b) and 7. A function that is continuous on an open set containing its topological support is continuous everywhere (ContinuousOn.continuous_of_tsupport_subset): at points of O use continuity on the open set O, and at points outside tsupport h, h vanishes on the open neighbourhood ℝ^P ∖ tsupport h. So h is continuous.
9. h agrees with γ on K. For x ∈ K, χ(x) = 1 by step 5(a), so h(x) = 1·γ(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
10. By steps 7–9, h is continuous, has compact support, and satisfies h(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) for every x ∈ K, as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: f and Df are continuous on the open set O (f is C¹), and (β, A) ↦ β∘A is jointly continuous (strict derivative), so γ = ω(f)∘Df is continuous on O.
Margin cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O, and a Urysohn cut-off χ with χ = 1 on K and compact tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O.
h := χ·γ satisfies tsupport h ⊆ tsupport χ, so h has compact support; h is continuous on the open set O ⊇ tsupport h, hence continuous; h = γ on K.

subproblems.title: Mollification: a continuous compactly supported covector field is a uniform limit of test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let h : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) n) be continuous with compact support. Then there is a sequence (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} of test forms ω_j ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n: C^∞ with compact support) converging to h uniformly on ℝ^P (TendstoUniformly, for the operator norm on Λⁿ(ℝ^P)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (h : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → ∃ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, TendstoUniformly (fun j x => (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) h atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof. These are the mollified smooth forms that approximate the continuous, compactly supported form β = χ·(ω(f(·))∘ΛⁿDf(·)) uniformly, behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 415–424: f_#T is well defined for C¹ f when T has locally finite mass). The same convolution is formalized in the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field (candidate commit 8abce32), whose Lean proof uses the API cited below. The parent needs only uniform convergence, so its support bound tsupport ω_j ⊆ tsupport h + B̄(0, 1) (step 3(a)) is not part of this statement.
Notation and setting: Λⁿ := Λⁿ(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n is a finite-dimensional real normed space (operator norm), hence complete; dist(α, β) = ‖α − β‖. ℝ^P carries Lebesgue measure (volume). For a scalar kernel ψ, (ψ ⋆ h)(x) := ∫ ψ(t)·h(x − t) dt; in Mathlib this is convolution ψ h (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, a Bochner integral in Λⁿ.
Formal remark: the frozen imports of GMT.Ch07.Submission include Mathlib.Analysis.Convolution, but not Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed or ...BumpFunction.Convolution. So ContDiffBump.normed and ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le are unavailable. The bump is normalized by hand (step 2), and the estimate uses dist_convolution_le (step 5).
1. h is uniformly continuous, because it is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). It is also locally integrable (Continuous.locallyIntegrable) and a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable).
2. Kernels. For j ∈ ℕ let r_j := 1/(j + 1) > 0, and let φ_j be the smooth bump function ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^P) with inner radius r_j/2 and outer radius r_j. Then:
 - φ_j is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff) and φ_j ≥ 0;
 - support φ_j = ball(0, r_j) (ContDiffBump.support_eq);
 - φ_j has compact support and is continuous, hence integrable.
 Since φ_j ≥ 0 and its support, an open ball, has positive Lebesgue measure (measure_ball_pos), c_j := ∫ φ_j > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg). Put ψ_j := φ_j / c_j. Then:
 - ψ_j is C^∞ (ContDiff.div_const) and ψ_j ≥ 0;
 - ∫ ψ_j = c_j / c_j = 1 (integral_div);
 - support ψ_j ⊆ support φ_j = ball(0, r_j);
 - ψ_j has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono).
3. Definition. ω_j := ψ_j ⋆ h, i.e. ω_j(x) = ∫ ψ_j(t)·h(x − t) dt.
4. ω_j is a test form.
 (a) ψ_j is C^∞ with compact support and h is locally integrable, so ω_j is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left, at smoothness order ∞).
 (b) ψ_j and h both have compact support, so ω_j does too (HasCompactSupport.convolution).
 (c) Hence IsTestForm ω_j, i.e. IsSmoothForm ω_j ∧ HasCompactSupport ω_j. Trivially tsupport ω_j ⊆ ℝ^P = univ, so ω_j ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
5. Pointwise estimate. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and η ≥ 0 with dist(h(y), h(x)) ≤ η for every y ∈ ball(x, r_j). Since ∫ ψ_j = 1, ω_j(x) − h(x) = ∫ ψ_j(t)·(h(x − t) − h(x)) dt. Since ψ_j ≥ 0 and ψ_j(t) = 0 unless ‖t‖ < r_j (i.e. x − t ∈ ball(x, r_j)), we get dist(ω_j(x), h(x)) ≤ ∫ ψ_j(t)·η dt = η. This is Mathlib's dist_convolution_le, applied with support ψ_j ⊆ ball(0, r_j), ψ_j ≥ 0, ∫ ψ_j = 1, and h a.e. strongly measurable.
6. Uniform convergence. Let ε > 0.
 - By step 1 there is δ > 0 with dist(h(y), h(x)) < ε/2 whenever dist(y, x) < δ (Metric.uniformContinuous_iff).
 - Choose J ∈ ℕ with 1/(J + 1) < δ (exists_nat_one_div_lt).
 - Let j ≥ J. Then r_j = 1/(j + 1) ≤ 1/(J + 1) < δ, so dist(h(y), h(x)) < ε/2 for every x and every y ∈ ball(x, r_j).
 - Step 5 with η = ε/2 gives dist(h(x), ω_j(x)) ≤ ε/2 < ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
 So for every ε > 0, eventually in j, dist(h(x), ω_j(x)) < ε for all x. By Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff this is TendstoUniformly (fun j x ↦ ω_j(x)) h atTop.
7. The sequence j ↦ ω_j ∈ TestFormOn univ n (step 4) satisfies TendstoUniformly (fun j x ↦ ω_j(x)) h atTop (step 6), as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: h is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous and locally integrable.
ψ_j = φ_j/∫φ_j for a smooth bump φ_j supported in ball(0, 1/(j+1)): ψ_j is C^∞, ψ_j ≥ 0, ∫ψ_j = 1, with compact support (manual normalization; ContDiffBump.normed is not imported).
ω_j = ψ_j ⋆ h is C^∞ with compact support, so ω_j ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
dist(ω_j(x), h(x)) ≤ sup over |t| < 1/(j+1) of dist(h(x − t), h(x)), which tends to 0 uniformly in x (dist_convolution_le plus uniform continuity).

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity integrals converge under uniform convergence on a compact set carrying the carrier
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), and K ⊆ U compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let g_j (j ∈ ℕ) and g be continuous maps ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) n) such that g_j → g uniformly on K. Then ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g_j(x)) dHⁿ(x) → ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)) dHⁿ(x) as j → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (gs : ℕ → Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ K) = 0 → (∀ j, Continuous (gs j)) → Continuous g → TendstoUniformlyOn gs g atTop K → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (gs j x) ∂μHE[n]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (g x) ∂μHE[n]))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–6 of the parent proof. They identify ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ with the limit of the integrals against uniformly approximating forms, as behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 415–424) for currents with the integral representation 2.7 (line 271). Three generalizations: the carrier fact Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0 with spt Y ⊆ K is replaced by the hypothesis Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0; the specific forms ω_j, h are replaced by arbitrary continuous g_j, g with g_j → g uniformly on K; and ℝ^P is replaced by an arbitrary U ⊇ K.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]. M := R.carrier, a measurable set. θ := R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, measurable. ξ := R.orient; ξ(x) ∈ MultiVector P n is a continuous linear functional on Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n. μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Λⁿ. F_j(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(g_j(x)) and F(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)). The claim is ∫F_j dμ → ∫F dμ, i.e. ∫_M θξ(g_j) dHⁿ → ∫_M θξ(g) dHⁿ.
1. μ-almost every point lies in K. Since M is measurable (R.measurableSet_carrier), ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ K is equivalent to Hⁿ{x : x ∈ M and x ∉ K} = 0 (ae_restrict_iff', ae_iff). That set is M ∖ K, which is Hⁿ-null by hypothesis.
2. Orientation bound. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. So there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) in ℝ^P with either ξ(x)(β) = β(τ) for all β ∈ Λⁿ, or ξ(x)(β) = −β(τ) for all β. At such x, for every β ∈ Λⁿ: |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; ‖τ_i‖ = 1 by orthonormality; for n = 0 the empty product is 1). Hence ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ β ∈ Λⁿ, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖.
3. θ is μ-integrable. Since K is compact and K ⊆ U, R.locallyIntegrable_mult gives c := ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. We have M ∖ (M ∩ K) = M ∖ K, which is Hⁿ-null, and (M ∩ K) ∖ M = ∅. So M and M ∩ K agree Hⁿ-a.e. (ae_eq_set), and μ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_congr_set). The function x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) ≥ 0 is measurable (measurable_from_nat composed with R.measurable_mult), and ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ = θ(x) (Real.enorm_natCast). So ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ dμ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ = c < ∞, and θ is μ-integrable (HasFiniteIntegral). Put Θ := ∫ θ dμ, a real number with Θ ≥ 0.
4. Measurability. Let G : ℝ^P → Λⁿ be continuous. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(G(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, because:
 - x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable;
 - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient);
 - G is continuous, hence strongly measurable;
 - the evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β), MultiVector P n × Λⁿ → ℝ, is bounded bilinear, hence continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply), so x ↦ ξ(x)(G(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂);
 - a product of a.e. strongly measurable real functions is a.e. strongly measurable.
 Lean remark: use Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply, as the accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub does. ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ does not unify with R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, because the topology instance on MultiVector P n differs syntactically.
5. Integrability. Let G : ℝ^P → Λⁿ be continuous. G is continuous on the compact set K, so there is C_G with ‖G(x)‖ ≤ C_G for x ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). For μ-a.e. x, x ∈ K (step 1) and the bound of step 2 holds. At such x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(G(x))| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(G(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖G(x)‖ ≤ C_G·θ(x). The function C_G·θ is μ-integrable (step 3), so with step 4, x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(G(x)) is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'). In particular every F_j and F is μ-integrable, since g_j and g are continuous.
6. Estimate. Let ε > 0 and put ε' := ε/(Θ + 1) > 0. Since g_j → g uniformly on K, there is J such that ‖g_j(x) − g(x)‖ = dist(g(x), g_j(x)) < ε' for all j ≥ J and all x ∈ K (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff). Fix j ≥ J. For μ-a.e. x (x ∈ K and the bound of step 2 holds), linearity of ξ(x) gives
 |F_j(x) − F(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(g_j(x) − g(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖g_j(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·ε'.
 Since F_j and F are μ-integrable (step 5), ∫F_j dμ − ∫F dμ = ∫(F_j − F) dμ (integral_sub). With the integrable bound θ·ε' (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le), |∫F_j dμ − ∫F dμ| ≤ ∫ θ·ε' dμ = Θ·ε/(Θ + 1) < ε (integral_mul_const; Θ ≥ 0).
7. So for every ε > 0 there is J with |∫F_j dμ − ∫F dμ| < ε for all j ≥ J. By Metric.tendsto_atTop, ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g_j(x)) dHⁿ(x) → ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)) dHⁿ(x) as j → ∞. ∎

R.orients gives |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ for μ-a.e. x (orthonormal τ, le_opNorm).
